in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information!

Since Alex is 17 years old, eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he is in approved education or training.

Could you please tell me if Alex is currently in any of the following:
- Full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or NVQs up to level 3)
- Approved training (such as a traineeship in England)
- Or has he left education/training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He actually left school recently, but he's just signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know!

That's helpful information. When a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training, you may still be able to claim Child Benefit for 20 weeks if they register with a government-sponsored careers service (or the armed services).

To confirm eligibility, I have a couple more questions:

1. Do you live in the UK?
2. Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. And yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that!

I just have a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

1. Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?
2. Is Alex working 24 hours or more per week, or receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. And no, he's not working - he just does a Saturday paper round, nothing like 24 hours a week. He doesn't get any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information! I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why you qualify:

**For Alex (age 17):**
- Although Alex has left education, he has registered with a government-sponsored careers service. This means you can continue to receive Child Benefit for **up to 20 weeks** from when he left education/training.
- You live in the UK and Alex lives with you, so you are responsible for him.
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.
- Alex is not working 24 hours or more per week and is not receiving benefits in his own right.

**Important things to note:**
- The 20-week period starts from when Alex left education/training, so be mindful of this timeframe.
- If Alex starts approved education or training, an apprenticeship, starts working 24+ hours per week, or begins receiving certain benefits, your eligibility may change, and you should notify HMRC.

If you haven't already made a claim, you can apply for Child Benefit through the official government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know?

All eligibility criteria are met for the 20-week extension period.
